questions.stem: An analyst has a 5-bit unsigned field. What is the maximum value?
questions.explanation: Five unsigned bits represent 0 to 31, so the maximum is 31. The count of values is 32.
questions.hint: Two to the fifth minus one.

questions.stem: An analyst compares BCD and pure binary for storing 99. Which uses more bits?

options.text: Both use 7 bits
BCD uses 8 bits while binary uses 7 bits
Binary uses 8 bits while BCD uses 7 bits
Both use 8 bits

questions.explanation: BCD uses two 4-bit fields for 99, totaling 8 bits, while pure binary 99 fits in 7 bits. BCD trades space for digit access.

stimulus.body: An analyst's dashboard note shows an 8-bit field. One version treats it as unsigned, the other as signed. The signed version's maximum positive value is much smaller.

questions.stem: Why is the signed maximum smaller?

options.text: The sign bit increases precision
Signed values are stored in decimal
One bit is reserved for the sign
Unsigned fields cannot hold negatives
options.misconception: states a true fact as the reason

questions.explanation: Reserving a bit for sign leaves fewer bits for magnitude, so the positive maximum drops. That is the cost of signed representation.
